draft.title: Evaluating with simile and metaphor
card: compares two things using like or as. Example: "The game was as slow as a wet Monday."
says one thing is another. Example: "The game was a snail race."
A review judges a text or event. A comparison can show the judgement through an image, so it carries a layer of meaning that a plain word such as boring does not.
The comparison also shows the writer's attitude. A rollercoaster suggests thrills, while a snail race suggests dullness.
draft.remember: A simile or metaphor lets a review judge through an image, adding meaning a plain judgement lacks.

a.q: A reviewer says a novel was "a thick fog I never found my way out of". What is the main effect of this comparison?
opts: It suggests the novel was confusing and hard to follow
It states that the novel is mostly about the weather
It shows the reviewer enjoyed the exciting plot twists
It compares the novel to another book by its title
a.why: Fog hides the way ahead, so the metaphor judges the novel as confusing. It is not about weather. Nothing in it suggests excitement.
a.clue: Think about what fog does to your view.

b.q: A reviewer says the band's new album is a warm blanket. What is this, and what does it judge?
opts: A metaphor that judges the album as comforting
A simile that judges the album as comforting
A metaphor that judges the album as loud and harsh
A simile that judges the album as dull and cold
b.why: The album is said to be a blanket without like or as, so it is a metaphor. A warm blanket suggests comfort. The simile option fails because there is no like or as.
b.clue: Check whether the sentence uses like or as.

a.best: It suggests the novel was confusing and hard to follow

b.best: A metaphor that judges the album as comforting
